***

**LOS ANGELES, California (CNN)** — Host Ryan Seacrest captured the essence of Tuesday night's *American Idol* finale perfectly as he introduced the show's top two finalists, Adam Lambert and Kris Allen. 

"It is the battle of the acoustic rocker versus the glam rocker," Seacrest declared. "Conway, Arkansas versus California. The guy next door versus the guy-liner."

Following three rounds of performances and extensive commentary from the judges, Southern California’s glam-rocker Adam Lambert appears to hold the advantage—though the night did not begin entirely in his favor.

In the opening round, which featured reprise performances chosen by the contestants, Simon Cowell declared Kris Allen the victor following his soulful piano rendition of "Ain't No Sunshine." [Watch Allen and Lambert talk after the show »] 

Lambert countered with a reprise of "Mad World," wearing a full-length black coat amidst a stage shrouded in white smoke—a staging choice Cowell criticized as "over-theatrical."

"I think 'Mad World' is kind of symbolic," Lambert reflected to reporters after the broadcast. "It talks about people who don't feel like they fit in."

The second round featured selections hand-picked by *American Idol* creator Simon Fuller. Shedding his dark overcoat for a sleek, reflective silver suit, Lambert delivered a powerhouse performance of Sam Cooke's "A Change Is Gonna Come." Judge Paula Abdul raved, calling it "the best I've ever heard you sing, ever!"

By contrast, Allen’s rendition of Marvin Gaye’s classic "What's Goin' On" met with considerably cooler feedback. [See the best and worst performances from season eight »]

"I thought it was too laid back for a night like this," noted Cowell, officially awarding the second round to Lambert.

The final round presented a shared challenge: both contestants were required to perform a original ballad co-written by judge Kara DioGuardi titled "No Boundaries." Lambert took the stage first, navigating the anthem with relative ease. Afterward, Cowell commended the 27-year-old, stating, "You have been one of the best, most original contestants we've ever had on the show."

Allen, on the other hand, noticeably struggled with pitch throughout his performance. Nevertheless, the panel offered a more encouraging response. "You have thoroughly, thoroughly deserved to be standing on that stage tonight, congratulations," Cowell affirmed. [Watch anchors debate "Idol" finalists »]

Speaking with reporters post-show, Lambert acknowledged the brief preparation time for the coronation song, describing it as "kind of a rush job." 

"There was a lot of lyric, and it was a big song," Lambert noted. "But it's a beautiful song."

The head-to-head finale feels remarkably fitting given the contestants' history. According to Allen, he and Lambert were roommates earlier in the competition and regularly offered each other constructive feedback. "He's always giving me stuff to change about mine... to make it better," Allen shared. [iReport.com: Who should win: Kris or Adam?]

Adding an extra element of drama to the evening, a 4.0-magnitude aftershock struck just 10 miles southeast of downtown Los Angeles a little over an hour before showtime. The broadcast was hosted live at the Nokia Theatre downtown, not far from the epicenter of a 4.7-magnitude earthquake that struck Sunday evening. However, to Allen's disappointment, neither finalist felt Tuesday's tremor. 

"I was totally upset, too, because I've never been to California (except for 'American Idol'), and I was like, 'I want to feel an earthquake,'" Allen joked.

Both Allen and Lambert will return to the stage Wednesday night for the two-hour season finale, where they—and viewers around the globe—will finally learn who will be crowned the next *American Idol*.

**(CNN) —** It is the classic *American Idol* matchup: the theatrical, octave-busting rocker against the understated, acoustic singer-songwriter. 

On Tuesday night, Adam Lambert and Kris Allen went head-to-head at the Nokia Theatre in Los Angeles for the final performance night of *American Idol* Season 8, delivering a three-round vocal duel that left the judges divided and host Ryan Seacrest predicting the closest vote in the show’s history.

With a record-breaking number of votes expected to be cast, both contestants fought to claim the title, tackling a song chosen by themselves, a song selected by show creator Simon Fuller, and the official winner's coronation single.

Here is how the final showdown played out:

### Round 1: Contestant's Choice

Kris Allen kicked off the evening by revisiting a fan favorite, stepping up to a grand piano for a soulful, stripped-down arrangement of Bill Withers’ "Ain't No Sunshine." The risk paid off immediately, setting a high bar for the night.

"There are a lot of people who doubted you being in the finals this week," said judge Randy Jackson. "That was one of your best performances ever."

Adam Lambert responded by bringing back his haunting, moody cover of Tears for Fears' "Mad World," descending a set of stairs bathed in blue light and shrouded in fog, dressed in a sweeping trench coat. 

While Paula Abdul dubbed the performance "brilliant," Simon Cowell offered a rare critique, suggesting the staging felt a bit "overly theatrical," though he admitted Lambert’s vocals were top-tier. 

[*Watch Kris Allen take on 'Ain't No Sunshine' »*](javascript:void(0))

### Round 2: Simon Fuller’s Choice

For the second round, creator Simon Fuller assigned the tracks. Allen was handed Marvin Gaye’s classic anthem "What’s Going On." Accompanied by his acoustic guitar and a back-porch rhythm section, Allen gave the track a laid-back, college-rock spin. 

The judges, however, were mixed. While Kara DioGuardi praised Allen for staying true to his artistry, Cowell was unimpressed, describing the arrangement as "like a guy with his mates sitting in a garage" and declaring that Allen had lost the round.

Lambert then took the stage with a show-stopping performance of Sam Cooke’s 1964 civil rights anthem, "A Change Is Gonna Come." Dressed in a sleek suit, Lambert leaned into his gospel and soul influences, climaxing in a series of his signature high-register shrieks.

"That was the best I’ve ever heard you sing," Abdul raved, visible tears in her eyes. 

Cowell agreed, declaring Lambert the clear winner of Round 2. 

[*Watch Adam Lambert perform 'A Change Is Gonna Come' »*](javascript:void(0))

### Round 3: The Winner’s Single

The final round saw both singers tackle "No Boundaries," a soaring pop-rock ballad co-written by judge Kara DioGuardi specifically for the finale. 

Allen went first, struggling slightly to project over the song's massive key changes. DioGuardi admitted after the performance that she may have written the key a bit too high, but praised Allen’s heart: "You are a brave soul. You have been a dark horse in this competition, and I am proud of you."

Lambert closed the night with his version of the track, effortlessly hitting the soaring notes, though the song itself drew muted reactions from the panel. Cowell bypassed analyzing the song entirely to offer a final tribute to both finalists.

"I think the point of this show is to find a global star," Cowell said, looking directly at Lambert. "I genuinely believe we’ve found that in you. But Kris, you earned your spot here tonight too."

[*Watch the finalists perform the coronation single 'No Boundaries' »*](javascript:void(0))

### The Final Verdict

Backstage after the show, both contestants appeared humbled by the overwhelming experience.

"I just wanted to leave everything I had out on that stage tonight," Lambert told reporters. "No matter what happens tomorrow, to have made it to this point feels like a total win."

Allen echoed the sentiment, acknowledging his underdog status throughout the season. "Whatever happens tomorrow, this has been an absolute dream," Allen said. "Adam is a force of nature, and just sharing the stage with him has been an honor."

The voting lines remained open for four hours following the broadcast. The winner of *American Idol* Season 8 will be crowned during Wednesday night's live two-hour finale, featuring guest performances by Queen, KISS, and Lionel Richie.

**SHOCKER IN HOLLYWOOD: Underdog Kris Allen Stuns Adam Lambert to Win 'American Idol' Season 8**

**LOS ANGELES (May 20, 2009)** — In one of the most stunning upsets in television history, soft-spoken Arkansas singer-songwriter Kris Allen was crowned the Season 8 champion of *American Idol* tonight, defeating the heavily favored vocal powerhouse Adam Lambert. 

Before a packed, screaming audience at the Nokia Theatre and nearly 100 million voters nationwide, host Ryan Seacrest announced the shocking result at the end of a jammed-packed, two-hour star-studded season finale. 

When his name was called, a visibly stunned Allen covered his face in disbelief. Looking bewildered by his own victory, the 23-year-old worship leader immediately bowed to his fellow finalist. 

"Adam deserves this," a humble Allen told Seacrest on stage, still struggling to process the news. "I’m sorry, I don’t even know what to feel right now. This is crazy."

Lambert, 27, who had dominated headlines, judge praise, and fan fervor all season with his theatrical style, jaw-dropping octave-leaping vocals, and bold fashion, took the runner-up finish with total grace. He immediately gave Allen a massive hug, smiling as the crowd erupted.

### A Battle of Contrasting Styles

The victory caps off a "David vs. Goliath" storyline that captivated the nation. 

Throughout the season, Lambert was widely considered the frontrunner. His haunting performance of Tears for Fears' "Mad World" and his blistering rendition of Led Zeppelin's "Whole Lotta Love" earned him universal acclaim and even a rare standing ovation from notoriously tough judge Simon Cowell.

Allen, meanwhile, quietly emerged as the ultimate dark horse. Armed with a guitar or sitting at a piano, his warm vocals and inventive, stripped-down arrangements—most notably his acoustic reinvention of Kanye West’s "Heartless"—steadily built him a massive fan base across middle America. 

On Tuesday night’s final performance showcase, the contrast was on full display. Lambert delivered a soul-stirring rendition of Sam Cooke’s "A Change Is Gonna Come," while Allen scored a knockout blow with a reprise of his soulful take on Bill Withers' "Ain't No Sunshine." Both singers struggled slightly with the soaring key changes of the co-written coronation song, "No Boundaries," but Allen’s understated approach seemed to resonate with voters looking for an accessible, radio-friendly artist.

### A Star-Studded Extravaganza

Tonight’s results show played less like a competition and more like a massive rock festival, featuring a dizzying array of A-list guest stars pairing up with the season's top contestants:

*   **Adam Lambert** fulfilled a lifelong rock-and-roll fantasy by taking the stage with legendary glam-rockers **KISS**, donning soaring platform boots and leather to belt out "Detroit Rock City" and "Rock and Roll All Nite."
*   **Kris Allen** teamed up with country superstar **Keith Urban** for an energetic, guitar-shredding performance of Urban's hit "Kiss a Girl."
*   Pop star **Katy Perry** showed her allegiance during her performance of "Waking Up in Vegas," wearing a cape emblazoned with Adam Lambert's name.
*   In one of the night’s most poignant moments, **both Lambert and Allen joined rock icons Queen** to perform the ultimate anthem, "We Are the Champions." Lambert’s soaring vocals alongside the legendary band left many wondering if a future collaboration might be in the card.

Other highlights included Steve Martin playing banjo with the Top 8 men, Lionel Richie performing with Danny Gokey, Cyndi Lauper duetting with Allison Iraheta, and appearances by Rod Stewart, Santana, and The Black Eyed Peas.

### The Aftermath

Despite Cowell admitting earlier in the night that he thought Lambert was the superior performer over the course of the season, the judge praised both men for their sportsmanship and talent. "To both of you, you were brilliant, charismatic, clean-cut, and great contestants," Cowell noted. 

With a record-breaking tally of nearly 100 million votes cast for the finale, Season 8 proved that *American Idol* remains the undisputed titan of American pop culture. 

While Kris Allen officially walks away with the record contract and the title—closing out the show with an emotional reprise of "No Boundaries"—industry insiders agree that both artists are bound for stardom. Allen’s humble, acoustic-pop sound is primed for mainstream radio, while Lambert’s undeniable star power and massive vocal range guarantee he will be a force in the music industry for years to come.

---

### Round 3: The Winner’s Single

The night concluded with both finalists attempting "No Boundaries," a soaring, highly demanding power ballad co-written by judge Kara DioGuardi.

In his final critique of the season, Cowell bypasses formal commentary on the song itself—which had been visibly difficult for both men—and instead addressed the contestants directly.

"Kris, you have been the absolute dark horse in this competition, and you earned your right to be on this stage tonight," Cowell said. Turning to Lambert, Cowell added: "The whole point of a show like this is to find a global star. You are undeniably one of the best performers we have ever had on this show."

---

### Backstage: The Finalists Speak

Minutes after the cameras stopped rolling—and as news of the Southern California earthquake began to circulate through the press room backstage—both finalists appeared relaxed, if visibly exhausted, by the whirlwind evening.

"Did the earth move for you guys, or was that just Adam's high notes?" Allen joked with reporters backstage when asked about the mid-show quake. 

Reflecting on his journey from dark horse to contender, Allen was pragmatic about his chances. "Going up against Adam all season has been intimidating, but tonight I just wanted to be myself," Allen told CNN. "Whatever happens tomorrow, I feel like I gave everything I had on that stage. If I lose to Adam, I’m losing to one of the best singers I’ve ever met."

Lambert, clad in his signature leather and glitter, was equally reflective about the night’s intense emotional rollercoaster. 

"I didn't even feel the earthquake, honestly—I had so much adrenaline pumping through my veins," Lambert confessed to CNN backstage. "For me, Round 2 singing Sam Cooke was the moment of the night. That song means so much to me musically. To have Simon say what he said... I couldn't ask for a better ending to this crazy ride."

---

### The Verdict Awaits

With the judges offering split decisions across the three rounds, the outcome now rests entirely in the hands of the voting public. Fox executives reported record-breaking call volumes immediately following the broadcast, signaling that Wednesday night's finale will be one of the closest votes in *American Idol* history.

Whether voters favor Lambert’s theatrical star power or Allen’s authentic, boy-next-door musicality, one thing is certain: on a night where the ground literally shook in Los Angeles, *American Idol* delivered a finale worthy of the seismic buzz surrounding it.
